inputs.source: HR maintained published policy documents returned by policy_search

controls.name: Read-only least-privilege credential scoped to the policy index
Reply destination is bound to the authenticated requester chat session
controls.decay_rationale: Destination comes from the authenticated chat session record rather than model-selected recipients, so the model cannot redirect replies to an attacker-controlled destination.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
Network egress denied at the runtime layer and verified by pen test
controls.decay_rationale: Runtime network policy blocks outbound destinations other than the bounded chat path; the runtime notes state this has been verified by pen test.

controls.name: Pinned model with change ticket required for model updates

findings.title: Bounded policy retrieval and reply path limits disclosure to the authenticated employee session

attack_path.note: Agent reads internal published policy content
Agent replies only into the authenticated requester's chat session

forecast.watch_signal: Any runtime or product change that stops binding chat replies to the authenticated requester record, widens the searchable corpus beyond published policies, or changes the agent purpose beyond HR policy QA requires reassessment.

evidence.observation: The prompt limits the agent to answering questions about published Acme HR policies and to using policy_search for relevant policy text.
The only declared tool is policy_search.search, which searches the published HR policy index.

The policy index holds only published policies with internal sensitivity, the agent credential is read only and scoped to that index, and replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session.
The chat client does not render images or auto fetch links, reducing hidden egress through reply rendering.

recommendations.action: Keep reply routing bound to the authenticated requester record and re-run assessment before any change that adds new recipients, channels, or searchable data sources.

findings.title: Trusted employee input can influence answer selection, but no untrusted source or open egress path is present in the reviewed design

attack_path.note: Authenticated employee prompt reaches reply generation
Agent returns a direct reply in the same authenticated chat session

forecast.watch_signal: If the design adds new external content sources, tools, or broader data access, reassess because the current low rating depends on the absence of untrusted inputs and the single bounded reply channel.

evidence.observation: The prompt is short and purpose-bound; no ambiguous delegation, self-modification, or broad authority is declared.
Only one read-only search tool is available; no execution, configuration, spend, delegation, or general network tools are declared.
The design states there is no memory and no network egress beyond the reply path to the authenticated requester's session.

recommendations.action: Preserve the current narrow scope: do not add external retrieval, memory, or additional outbound channels without reassessment.

rating.rationale: Present-path inherent risk is moderate because a trusted employee can cause the agent to read internal policy content and return it through an irreversible reply channel. Residual drops to low because the reviewed design structurally severs broader disclosure paths: replies are bound to the authenticated requester session, searchable content is limited to published internal policies, credentials are read-only and scoped, and runtime network egress is denied and reportedly pen-tested. Forecast rises to moderate if destination binding or current scope constraints are removed or broadened.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt, tool manifest, and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, IaC, or live runtime configuration was provided, so implementation details such as exact chat-session binding enforcement and network policy rules were assessed from declarations rather than direct inspection.
Manual validation was applied against the provided schema and validation checklist because scripts could not be run in this environment.
